final_rationale: The verdict changes because the Actor narrowed the position to a conditional, policy-bounded claim and expressly conceded the unresolved predicates; no new admissible evidence was added. On that narrower reading, the Actor is no longer claiming that rollout controls alone cure the weakness or that the present record proves current launch compliance. That caveated position is supported by admissible evidence: aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support release-level readiness, while policy and rollout evidence require explicit disclosure, exclusion of the exposed use case, or approved risk acceptance before launch. This is enough for compliant_with_caveats because the audited position is a conditional recommendation tied to a required pre-launch disclosure step. It is not fully compliant because the record still lacks evidence that the disclosure condition has actually been satisfied.
remaining_concerns: The record still does not show that the required model-card disclosure for the energy outage response limitation has been completed before launch.
The affected energy outage response segment remains exposed in the 9% initial rollout and is below target on the relevant task.
Rollout controls, rollback capability, and monitoring do not satisfy the disclosure requirement while the affected use case remains exposed.
The risk acceptance document is still only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the exposed outage segment.
If certification were executed now without disclosure completion, exclusion of the use case, or approved risk acceptance, the action would not satisfy policy.
